issues.description: Method Farm.singFarmSongVerse: the UML in problem_statement.md declares singFarmSongVerse as private with an Animal parameter (singFarmSongVerse(animal):void). The template repository declares a private singFarmSongVerse method but its parameter is commented out in the signature (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)) making the intended parameter unclear. The solution repository implements the method as protected with an Animal parameter (protected void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)). This visibility/signature mismatch can confuse students about the intended access level and required parameter, and may lead to inconsistent implementations or access issues if tests or subclass/package code expect protected access.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the visibility and signature across artifacts. Preferred fix (A): change the solution method to match the UML and template by using a private signature with the Animal parameter: private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and keep the method body as in the solution. Also update the template stub to include the parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) so students see the correct signature. Alternative fix (B): if protected access is intentional, update the problem_statement UML to show protected visibility and change the template method to protected void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). Ensure whichever option is chosen is applied consistently in problem_statement.md, the template file, and the solution file.
